candidateGrammar.explanation: For completed past actions like these, use the present of avoir plus a past participle: j’ai étudié, Ana a acheté, nous avons mangé, mes amis ont parlé. Regular -er verbs form -é (parler → parlé, étudier → étudié, acheter → acheté, manger → mangé). A regular -ir verb like finir forms -i (finir → fini). Écrire has the irregular past participle écrit. To ask a question, put est-ce que in front: Est-ce que tu as fini les devoirs hier ?

model.study: Hier, j’ai étudié à la bibliothèque.
model.eat: Nous avons mangé à la cafétéria.

candidateGrammar.caution: The passé composé looks like English “I have studied”, but it is also the normal way to say “I studied”: j’ai étudié can express both. A French question does not need English “did”: Est-ce que tu as fini… ? In these sentences, étudié, acheté, mangé, parlé and fini are regular; écrit is irregular. With avoir in these examples, participles do not change with a feminine or plural subject: Ana a acheté, mes amis ont parlé.
